children: Alimentation Couche-Tard is scheduled to release its fiscal first-quarter results on Tuesday after markets close. Here's what you need to know.
REVENUE: According to a poll FactSet, analysts expect revenue to rise to $20.86 billion from $17.35 billion in the prior-year period.
EARNINGS PER SHARE: Analysts project earnings per share rise to 88 cents a share, up from 82 cents a share.
ADJUSTED EPS: On an adjusted basis, per-share earnings are pegged at 89 cents.
In the quarter, the stock rose 14% and recently traded at 83.16 Canadian dollars ($59.80).

-The Canadian convenience-store operator could be feeling the pinch of a more budget-conscious U.S. consumer. Stifel analyst Martin Landry says merchandise same-store sales in the U.S. could disappoint investors, pointing to a slowdown in performance among Couche-Tard's peers. Lower cigarette sales, in particular, could be the biggest drag in the quarter, which was the case with rival Murphy USA, the analyst said.

-Investors will be keen to know how easing volatility in crude oil will affect the business this quarter. RBC analyst Irene Nattel expects the phenomenon of last quarter, marked by swings in crude oil prices due to the conflict in Iran, to continue. She sees U.S. fuel margin at 48.75 cents a gallon, a 6.5 cent premium to industry margin, "as significant fuel price volatility amid the geopolitical situation."

-After abandoning its $47 billion takeover dream of the Japanese parent of 7-Eleven, Couche-Tard agreed to acquire Poland's largest convenience retailer Zabka for about $8.7 billion. RBC's Nattel expects management to share more details about the acquisition such as timelines and how it plans to integrate the new network into its own. "Forecasts do not incorporate the Zabka transaction pending clarity on ultimate ownership percentage once the tender offer concludes," she says in a report.
